case: United States v. Deaton; judgment below, 332 F.3d 698
result: Affirmed on statutory coverage, constitutional authority, delineation and restoration, 9–0; Kennedy delivers the complete lead, with the Chief’s differentiated joins.
chronology: The Fourth Circuit affirmed the Clean Water Act jurisdiction, wetland determination and restoration order in this second appeal on June 12, 2003. The Supreme Court matter is submitted on the merits and scheduled for December 11, 2003. No separate Supreme Court argument date is supplied. The earlier appellate determination that sidecasting was a discharge is settled. The owners seek relief from the statutory and constitutional application, the hydrology determination and the restoration method; the United States seeks affirmance.
participation: All nine participate at merits submission and decision; no case-specific absence is established. Nine satisfies the six-member quorum, with five votes needed. The supplied proper-before-the-Court premise governs. The Chief supports all four disposition components but has the differentiated opinion joins stated below.
reach: The four preserved components receive separate grounds: statutory delegation/coverage and regulatory interpretation; constitutional channel protection; the asserted Manual/hydrology error; and the independently challenged restoration method. The settled sidecasting issue is not reopened. The Manual-invalidity theory was not preserved, distinct from the presented argument that the Corps misapplied it.
entering: The actual SWANCC excludes bird-use-only jurisdiction over the isolated ponds there and retains Riverside Bayview’s adjacent-wetland construction without a universal present-navigability requirement. Haggar and Mead require actual delegation and exercise before controlling statutory deference. Auer separately governs the responsible agency’s fair, considered construction of its regulation; the Chief did not join that interpretive rule. Lopez preserves channel protection and demands a connection before aggregation. Home Builders has distinct substantial-externality requirements; Holston and Ho apply distinct supported market mechanisms. Barnhart materially confirms delegation-before-deference rather than transferring its separate statutory source to the Corps.
stone_test: Approved Section II supports the conclusion that these demonstrated tributary-connected wetlands fall within the Act, the complete channels rationale, the ordinary civil proof burdens and the restoration mandate. It does not supply the detailed Chevron/Mead/Auer reasoning or the separate restoration-alternative rationale. The Chief therefore joins the statutory coverage proposition, the full channels holding and the operative restoration mandate, without being counted for those unexpressed additional rationales. This is limited assent, not an invented affirmative objection. The separate wetland-delineation component is genuinely silent in Section II: the standing approved fallback supplies only the Chief’s vote to affirm that component, with no added ground. His explicit restoration position receives no fallback. No separate Chief writing is needed because the Court’s holdings and topology accurately state his supported grounds, qualifications and remedy. The externality requirements remain distinct; no second sufficient externality ground is attributed to him. His boundary concerning intermittent, remote or isolated waters lacking this demonstrated connection does not deny the actual disputed amount and consistency of flow along the agreed route.

public.Event: United States v. Deaton; judgment below, 332 F.3d 698. Merits decision, December 11, 2003, on merits submission. The Court reviews the Fourth Circuit’s affirmance of Clean Water Act jurisdiction, the wetland determination and an order to refill the excavated ditch and restore previolation elevation. The questions concern statutory coverage of wetlands adjoining the demonstrated tributary system, Congress’s channel-protection power, the Corps’ hydrology method and the restoration alternative. The earlier sidecasting-discharge ruling is settled. The wetlands adjoin a roadside ditch draining through a culvert, the John Adkins Prong of Perdue Creek and Beaverdam Creek to the navigable Wicomico River and Chesapeake Bay. The route is agreed; the amount and consistency of flow are disputed.

public.Holdings:
### I. The Act and valid regulations reach this connected system

**Controlling proposition:** The Clean Water Act and the Corps’ tributary and adjacent-wetland regulations cover these wetlands adjoining the demonstrated feeder system into navigable waters. The statutory program delegates authority exercised through binding regulations; the permissible inclusion of this connected system and the responsible Corps construction of tributaries as its feeder branches receive their respective controlling weight within statutory and regulatory limits.

**Authority:** Part I’s coverage conclusion has nine joins. Stevens, O’Connor, Scalia, Kennedy, Souter, Thomas, Ginsburg and Breyer supply eight direct joins to the complete delegated-choice and regulatory-interpretation rationale; Stone-Zsela’s join is confined to the coverage conclusion.

**Controlling explanation:** Sections 1311, 1344 and 1362 establish the discharge prohibition, dredged-or-fill permit program and definition extending beyond navigability in fact. Section 1344 assigns the program to the Secretary of the Army acting through the Chief of Engineers, with structured permit, guideline, general-permit and state-administration provisions. Haggar and Mead require that actual assignment and its exercise before deference; Barnhart applies the same sequence in a different statutory program. Ambiguity or expertise alone does not confer authority.

The Corps reasonably includes this connected tributary system and its conceded adjacent wetlands under section 328.3(a)(1), (5) and (7). The latter provision covers wetlands adjacent to the identified waters other than waters themselves wetlands. Riverside Bayview preserves adjacent-wetland coverage. SWANCC’s bird-use-only isolated-pond limit does not impose the owners’ proposed direct-feeder boundary on this supported connection.

The distinct question about the regulation’s meaning receives Auer’s fair-and-considered-interpretation rule. Tributaries reasonably includes feeder branches reaching navigable water through intermediate streams; the responsible Corps construction is consistent with that text. Earlier primary, secondary and tertiary usage confirms the meaning. A former headwaters coverage cutoff did not establish that more remote branches were linguistically never tributaries. The direct-feeder alternative is plausible but not compelled. Neither form of deference proves hydrological facts, permits interpretive amendment or displaces the Government’s ordinary civil burdens. The actual route and conceded adjacency supply the application here, rather than environmental importance alone.

### II. Protection of the receiving navigable channel supports this application

**Controlling proposition:** Congress may prevent pollutant effects in an identified navigable waterway by regulating the established discharge class in its demonstrated tributary system and adjacent wetlands. The Government must support that connection and mechanism; once established, the channel ground requires neither an independently substantial effect from this individual fill nor tracing a particular particle into the receiving river.

**Authority:** Part II, joined by all nine Justices.

**Controlling explanation:** Lopez preserves direct protection of interstate channels and requires a real connection before aggregate magnitude can do work. Rio Grande Dam, Appalachian Electric Power, Oklahoma ex rel. Phillips and Grand River Dam support protection of navigable waters through relevant nonnavigable reaches; Caminetti recognizes protection against harmful channel uses. The power is not confined to clearing obstructions from boat passage.

The agreed drainage route connects the roadside ditch and adjacent wetlands to the Wicomico. The Corps supplied evidence that discharges into the connected tributaries and adjacent wetlands substantially affect receiving-water quality; the owners did not contend that the reported class effect was overstated. The approximately eight-mile route to the navigable river, intermediate ponds and dams, and disputed flow consistency therefore require attention but do not erase this supported connection. A particular parcel’s small contribution does not defeat prevention directed to that connected class.

The owners’ strongest objection is that remote drainage can turn channel protection into general land-use power. The answer is the established receiving channel, actual route and supported discharge mechanism, rather than a presumption that every ditch connects or national environmental concern. Home Builders retains a separate externality route. The externality route requires identification of the regulated class; a concrete cross-border ecological, commercial or comparable interstate effect; why that effect is substantial rather than speculative or merely nationally interesting; why the affected States cannot reasonably internalize or control it through ordinary territorial authority; and the reasonable fit of the federal prohibition to that effect. Drainage alone does not establish those conditions. The supported channel ground fully sustains this application.

### III. The root-zone indicator answers the preserved Manual objection

**Controlling proposition:** Section 328.3(b) requires inundation or saturation by surface or groundwater at a frequency and duration sufficient to support, and under normal circumstances actually supporting, a prevalence of vegetation typically adapted to saturated soils. Within that complete definition, the Manual’s express visual indicator of saturation in a major part of the root zone, usually within twelve inches, defeats the asserted requirement of saturation to the surface; the Corps’ determination is sustained on this preserved interpretation issue.

**Authority:** Part III, joined by all eight Associate Justices. Stone-Zsela concurs in affirmance of this component without adding a ground.

**Controlling explanation:** The 1987 Manual applies vegetation, hydric-soil and hydrology criteria, with recorded water data ranked above field indicators. Its specific root-zone indicator explains how saturation can have the overriding effect on vegetation relevant to wetland hydrology. The owners’ twenty-two-well monitoring argument relied on inadequate saturation to the surface. Reading the general surface description with the express indicator answers their contention that the Corps contradicted the Manual. Vegetation and hydric soil are undisputed, and the described challenge establishes no contrary root-zone measurement requiring this Court to resolve a factual conflict.

Auer permits the responsible, text-consistent regulatory explanation; it does not allow a scientific manual to amend the regulation or make one observation conclusive. Frequency, duration, normal circumstances and the actual vegetation criterion remain essential. Genuinely contrary higher-ranked data must retain their proper weight. The claim that the Manual itself is inconsistent with the regulation was not presented. Affirmance thus resolves the asserted misuse of its language while preserving the complete regulatory conditions.

### IV. Refilling reasonably restores the established violation’s effects

**Controlling proposition:** A restoration order must bear an equitable relationship to the actual violation, be practically achievable and serve restoration of the affected environment. The district court did not abuse its discretion by requiring refilling and previolation elevation rather than removal of the sidecast soil elsewhere, because the proposed removal would preserve the unlawful project’s drainage benefit and risk further ecological harm.

**Authority:** Part IV’s complete rationale has the eight Associate joins. All nine support the operative restoration mandate; Stone-Zsela’s agreement is confined to that operative remedial scope.

**Controlling explanation:** The owners emphasize that digging alone was not the established discharge and that hauling the soil to nonwetland land could have avoided a violation initially. But an option that would have avoided a violation before the work does not necessarily restore the affected wetlands afterward. The actual findings explain both the retained drainage benefit and the risk of further harm from the proposed removal. Those concrete reasons connect the ordered refilling to the previolation condition.

Cumberland Farms supplies persuasive considerations of environmental benefit, feasibility and equitable relation rather than a compulsory checklist. The Act’s restoration objective supports the properly bounded choice; it does not establish a separate prohibition on excavation or authority over unrelated land use. The existing order remains tied to this discharge and its effects, and ordinary enforcement must address any supported feasibility or compliance issue on its evidence.
public.Precedent Treatment:
- United States v. Riverside Bayview Homes: applied to adjacent-wetland coverage within the enacted water program.
- Solid Waste Agency of Northern Cook County v. United States Army Corps of Engineers: distinguished because this application rests on a demonstrated tributary connection, preserving its bird-use-only isolated-pond limit.
- United States v. Haggar Apparel Co.: applied to actual delegated authority and independent enforcement of statutory limits before controlling deference.
- United States v. Mead Corp.: applied to actual delegation and its exercise through a mechanism carrying the force of law before controlling deference.
- Barnhart v. Thomas: applied to that delegation-first sequence without transferring its Social Security statutory assignment to the Corps.
- Auer v. Robbins: applied separately to the responsible, fair and text-consistent regulatory construction, preserving the distinction between interpretation and factual proof.
- United States v. Lopez: applied to the direct channel-protection ground and the need for a supported connection before aggregation.
- United States v. Rio Grande Dam & Irrigation Co.: applied to protection of navigable water against upstream interference.
- United States v. Appalachian Electric Power Co.: applied to protection of navigable waters through relevant nonnavigable reaches.
- Oklahoma ex rel. Phillips v. Guy F. Atkinson Co.: applied to protection of navigable waters through relevant nonnavigable reaches.
- United States v. Grand River Dam Authority: applied to protection of navigable waters through relevant nonnavigable reaches.
- Caminetti v. United States: applied to protection of navigable channels against harmful uses.
- National Association of Home Builders v. Babbitt: its separate interstate-externality requirements remain effective; the channel ground independently resolves this application.
public.Law After Decision: The demonstrated tributary system and its adjacent wetlands fall within the valid water program, and supported protection of the navigable receiving channel sustains this discharge application. Statutory delegation, regulatory interpretation, factual hydrology and constitutional authority remain distinct inquiries. The complete wetland definition continues to govern use of the root-zone indicator. Restoration requires its own equitable and practical justification, supplied here by the actual findings supporting refilling.
public.Procedure After Action: The affirmed restoration order remains enforceable under the district court’s actual terms, schedule and oversight. The owners must refill the ditch and restore previolation elevation as ordered. Supported questions about feasibility or compliance must be resolved from the order and the evidence in ordinary enforcement.

author: Kennedy
assignment: Kennedy is selected from the permitted balance pool. His actual Haggar and Mead opinions supply the delegation-before-deference sequence, and his Auer opinion supplies the distinct own-regulation inquiry that carries both coverage and the preserved Manual issue. Those are the central drafting tasks separating this opinion from the lower court’s ambiguity-alone formulation. Stevens, with one lead, is the strongest balance alternative: his full joins support every ground and his broader aquatic-protection position is compatible with this narrower channel ground. Kennedy’s two leads remain within the minimum-plus-one pool, and his demonstrated authorship of the three controlling interpretive frameworks provides the concrete case-specific reason to select him. The Chief’s judgment support cannot cure his lack of the complete rationale and does not make him eligible.
law_screen: The actual December 10 McConnell public holdings, final Greenville completeness copy and final Virginia completeness copy were screened against D1–D4. The clean final-public-law model receipt confirms no Associate change. McConnell’s election-specific affirmative sources and independent speech fit do not alter the supported channel category; its Barnhart treatment reinforces actual delegation before deference. Greenville retains each distinct operative standard. Virginia’s interstate instrument and complete fisheries savings do not alter the federal water program. The internal Holston/Ho and Virginia scope comparisons supply no independently required public holding and have therefore been omitted from the public five-block treatment. All eight Associates retain their frozen grounds, and the Chief’s complete supported joins and sole delineation fallback remain as tested above.
affected_later: This screen was performed only after D1–D4 and their joins were fixed and uses the five later decisions solely to identify consequences. Rancho Viejo (February 5, 2004) regulates the enacted wildlife-taking class under Home Builders, with an existing-record mechanism inquiry. Deaton’s demonstrated water connection and supported prevention of effects in an identified navigable channel supply neither a wildlife-market relationship nor an ecological externality for Rancho; its premise and remand are not displaced. Environmental Defense Center (March 25) concerns municipal own-discharge operations, an actual alternative to third-party administration and independently justified operational information. Deaton confirms a distinct connected-water application; it supplies neither EDC’s alternative permit nor its expression rationale, and displaces no EDC ground or administrative remand. Lomont (March 11) retains concrete official injury and unconditional refusal of certification; ACLU of New Jersey (April 13) retains its own custody-and-records delegation, separate APA exceptions and accepted-operation ground; West Virginia v. HHS (June 16) retains its related funding condition, complete beneficiary protections and genuine-practical-choice review. Deaton changes no necessary premise of those three decisions. No completed later Record requires reopening or correction, and none of these future holdings entered the present merits.
